allFrames.title: Handshake traffic secrets become available
allFrames.summary: ECDHE feeds the Handshake Secret; transcript(ClientHello…ServerHello) contextualizes client/server handshake traffic secrets.
allFrames.detail: HOPSCOTCH represents this symbolically. It does not fabricate secret bytes. These handshake traffic secrets protect the encrypted authentication flight that follows.

allFrames.title: Server authenticates the handshake transcript
allFrames.summary: Server Finished verifies the handshake state and completes the server authentication block.
allFrames.detail: Finished is a MAC over the transcript using a key derived from the server handshake traffic secret. The client must verify it before trusting the completed server handshake.

allFrames.title: Master and application traffic secrets are derived
allFrames.summary: The transcript through server Finished feeds client/server application traffic secret 0.
allFrames.detail: TLS 1.3 derives application traffic secrets from the Master Secret and the transcript through the server Finished. The client still has one handshake-authentication message left to send.

allFrames.title: The lanes visibly diverge
allFrames.summary: HTTP/2 stalls both responses; HTTP/3 keeps /app.js moving.

event.title: The lanes visibly diverge
event.summary: HTTP/2 stalls both responses; HTTP/3 keeps /app.js moving.
event.detail: TCP presents one ordered byte stream, so a sequence gap prevents later connection bytes from reaching HTTP/2. QUIC has no ordering relationship between bytes on different streams, so Stream B can progress while Stream A waits for repair.
event.h2Label: CONNECTION HOL · Stream A + Stream B blocked
event.h3Label: Stream A blocked · Stream B still progressing

event.h2Label: TCP retransmission repairs the connection byte stream
event.h3Label: Stream B has already moved ahead

allFrames.title: HTTP/2 releases both stalled streams

event.title: HTTP/2 releases both stalled streams
event.summary: /hero.jpg and /app.js jump forward together after TCP repair.
event.detail: This is transport head-of-line blocking beneath HTTP/2 multiplexing: independent HTTP streams were coupled by the ordered TCP substrate.
event.h2Label: Buffered H2 frames become deliverable
event.h3Label: No equivalent cross-stream release event was necessary

allFrames.title: QUIC repairs Stream A

event.title: QUIC repairs Stream A
event.summary: /hero.jpg receives the missing stream range while /app.js is already near completion.
event.detail: QUIC retransmits stream data as needed, but the lost Stream A range does not impose ordering on Stream B. STREAM frame boundaries need not be preserved during retransmission.
event.h2Label: Both H2 streams are progressing again
event.h3Label: Only Stream A needed ordering repair

allFrames.title: Both lanes complete
allFrames.summary: The final payload bytes are the same; the delivery coupling under loss was not.

event.title: Both lanes complete
event.summary: The final payload bytes are the same; the delivery coupling under loss was not.
event.detail: This theater isolates transport head-of-line behavior. It does not claim HTTP/3 can never block: flow control, congestion control, or QPACK dependencies can still create delays. This curated trace avoids dynamic QPACK dependencies.
event.h2Label: HTTP/2 complete after connection-level repair
event.h3Label: HTTP/3 complete with independent stream progress

allFrames.title: Connection established

allFrames.detail: The final ACK confirms both initial sequence numbers. Application data can now begin at client SEQ 1001.

event.title: Connection established
event.summary: ACK 7001 completes the three-way handshake.
event.detail: The final ACK confirms both initial sequence numbers. Application data can now begin at client SEQ 1001.

allFrames.title: Segment 1 arrives in order
allFrames.summary: SEQ 1001–2460 advances the receiver next-expected byte to 2461.
allFrames.detail: One full 1460-byte MSS arrives. The receiver is now waiting for byte 2461.

event.title: Segment 1 arrives in order
event.summary: SEQ 1001–2460 advances the receiver next-expected byte to 2461.
event.detail: One full 1460-byte MSS arrives. The receiver is now waiting for byte 2461.

allFrames.title: Segment 2 is lost
allFrames.summary: SEQ 2461–3920 disappears before the server receives it.
allFrames.detail: This missing sequence range creates a hole. TCP can recover it without waiting for the retransmission timer if enough later data arrives to produce duplicate ACKs.

event.title: Segment 2 is lost
event.summary: SEQ 2461–3920 disappears before the server receives it.
event.detail: This missing sequence range creates a hole. TCP can recover it without waiting for the retransmission timer if enough later data arrives to produce duplicate ACKs.

allFrames.title: Segment 3 arrives out of order
allFrames.summary: SEQ 3921–5380 arrives, but byte 2461 is still missing.
allFrames.detail: The receiver can buffer this later range, but its cumulative acknowledgment cannot move past the missing byte.

event.title: Segment 3 arrives out of order
event.summary: SEQ 3921–5380 arrives, but byte 2461 is still missing.
event.detail: The receiver can buffer this later range, but its cumulative acknowledgment cannot move past the missing byte.

allFrames.title: Duplicate ACK 1
allFrames.summary: The server repeats ACK 2461: that is still the first missing byte.
allFrames.detail: A duplicate cumulative ACK is evidence that later data arrived while the expected sequence did not.

event.title: Duplicate ACK 1
event.summary: The server repeats ACK 2461: that is still the first missing byte.
event.detail: A duplicate cumulative ACK is evidence that later data arrived while the expected sequence did not.

allFrames.title: Segment 4 extends the out-of-order queue
allFrames.summary: SEQ 5381–6840 arrives while the 2461 hole remains.
allFrames.detail: The receiver still cannot advance its cumulative ACK, so another duplicate ACK follows.

event.title: Segment 4 extends the out-of-order queue
event.summary: SEQ 5381–6840 arrives while the 2461 hole remains.
event.detail: The receiver still cannot advance its cumulative ACK, so another duplicate ACK follows.

allFrames.title: Duplicate ACK 2
allFrames.summary: ACK 2461 repeats again.
allFrames.detail: Two duplicate ACKs strengthen the loss signal, but this curated Reno scenario waits for the third duplicate ACK before fast retransmit.

event.title: Duplicate ACK 2
event.summary: ACK 2461 repeats again.
event.detail: Two duplicate ACKs strengthen the loss signal, but this curated Reno scenario waits for the third duplicate ACK before fast retransmit.

allFrames.title: Segment 5 arrives behind the same hole
allFrames.summary: SEQ 6841–8300 arrives out of order.
allFrames.detail: The receiver now holds three contiguous later segments behind the missing SEQ 2461–3920 range.

event.title: Segment 5 arrives behind the same hole
event.summary: SEQ 6841–8300 arrives out of order.
event.detail: The receiver now holds three contiguous later segments behind the missing SEQ 2461–3920 range.

allFrames.title: Duplicate ACK 3 triggers fast retransmit
allFrames.summary: The third ACK 2461 crosses the curated Reno fast-retransmit threshold.
allFrames.detail: The sender infers one segment was probably lost while the path still delivers later packets. It can retransmit without waiting for the retransmission timeout.

event.title: Duplicate ACK 3 triggers fast retransmit
event.summary: The third ACK 2461 crosses the curated Reno fast-retransmit threshold.
event.detail: The sender infers one segment was probably lost while the path still delivers later packets. It can retransmit without waiting for the retransmission timeout.

allFrames.title: Reno enters fast recovery
allFrames.summary: ssthresh falls to 3 MSS; cwnd is temporarily inflated to 6 MSS.
allFrames.detail: For this curated Reno model, the 6-MSS flight is halved to a 3-MSS slow-start threshold. During fast recovery, cwnd is represented as ssthresh + 3 duplicate ACKs = 6 MSS.

event.title: Reno enters fast recovery
event.summary: ssthresh falls to 3 MSS; cwnd is temporarily inflated to 6 MSS.
event.detail: For this curated Reno model, the 6-MSS flight is halved to a 3-MSS slow-start threshold. During fast recovery, cwnd is represented as ssthresh + 3 duplicate ACKs = 6 MSS.

allFrames.title: Fast retransmit repairs the hole
allFrames.summary: SEQ 2461–3920 is sent again immediately.
allFrames.detail: The retransmission carries the exact sequence range identified by the repeated ACK 2461 signal.

event.title: Fast retransmit repairs the hole
event.summary: SEQ 2461–3920 is sent again immediately.
event.detail: The retransmission carries the exact sequence range identified by the repeated ACK 2461 signal.

allFrames.title: One ACK releases the buffered ranges
allFrames.summary: ACK 8301 cumulatively covers segments 2 through 5.
allFrames.detail: Once the missing bytes arrive, the receiver already has SEQ 3921–8300 buffered. Its cumulative ACK can jump directly from 2461 to 8301.

event.title: One ACK releases the buffered ranges
event.summary: ACK 8301 cumulatively covers segments 2 through 5.
event.detail: Once the missing bytes arrive, the receiver already has SEQ 3921–8300 buffered. Its cumulative ACK can jump directly from 2461 to 8301.

allFrames.title: cwnd deflates to ssthresh
allFrames.summary: Fast recovery ends at cwnd 3 MSS, ssthresh 3 MSS.
allFrames.detail: The full cumulative ACK confirms recovery of the lost range. This curated Reno model exits fast recovery by deflating cwnd to the 3-MSS threshold.

event.title: cwnd deflates to ssthresh
event.summary: Fast recovery ends at cwnd 3 MSS, ssthresh 3 MSS.
event.detail: The full cumulative ACK confirms recovery of the lost range. This curated Reno model exits fast recovery by deflating cwnd to the 3-MSS threshold.

allFrames.title: Forward progress resumes
allFrames.summary: SEQ 8301–9760 crosses the repaired connection.
allFrames.detail: The sender continues from the cumulatively acknowledged sequence point instead of replaying data that the receiver already buffered.

event.title: Forward progress resumes
event.summary: SEQ 8301–9760 crosses the repaired connection.
event.detail: The sender continues from the cumulatively acknowledged sequence point instead of replaying data that the receiver already buffered.

allFrames.title: ACK 9761 grows the window again
allFrames.summary: Successful delivery raises the illustrated congestion window to 4 MSS.
allFrames.detail: The scenario now shows additive recovery rather than snapping immediately back to the pre-loss window.

event.title: ACK 9761 grows the window again

event.detail: The scenario now shows additive recovery rather than snapping immediately back to the pre-loss window.

frame.title: Primary link fails
frame.summary: The R1 ↔ CORE adjacency disappears and the forwarding path is broken.
frame.detail: Traffic can no longer traverse the installed primary route. The physical failure is immediate; control-plane convergence is not.

allFrames.title: Primary path established
allFrames.summary: Application traffic is flowing through R1 on the lowest-cost route.
allFrames.detail: The edge router prefers CLIENT → EDGE → R1 → CORE → APP with total metric 22. R2 remains a valid but more expensive standby path.

allFrames.title: Failure knowledge propagates
allFrames.summary: R2 and CORE now share the updated topology view.
allFrames.detail: The link-state database converges across the surviving path. Once the relevant routers have the same topology, shortest-path calculation can produce a replacement route.

payload.title: Failure knowledge propagates

allFrames.title: SPF selects the alternate path
allFrames.summary: The failed edge is removed from the graph and the standby route through R2 wins.
allFrames.detail: CLIENT → EDGE → R2 → CORE → APP is more expensive than the original route, but it is now the lowest-cost viable path.

payload.title: SPF selects the alternate path

allFrames.title: Forwarding moves to R2
allFrames.summary: New traffic leaves the edge router on the alternate next hop.
allFrames.detail: The forwarding plane installs the replacement route. The route exists again, but the application still has to absorb the disruption that occurred during convergence.

frame.summary: The answer is not here; the next authority is the test. TLD.
frame.detail: This is a referral, not the final A answer. It tells the recursive resolver which nameserver is authoritative for the next delegation step.

event.title: Root refers the resolver to .test
event.summary: The answer is not here; the next authority is the test. TLD.
event.detail: This is a referral, not the final A answer. It tells the recursive resolver which nameserver is authoritative for the next delegation step.

allFrames.title: Stub asks for a recursive answer
allFrames.summary: www.example.test A leaves the client with RD=1.
allFrames.detail: The application-facing stub resolver asks its configured recursive resolver to finish the job. Recursion Desired is set on this client-to-resolver query.

event.title: Stub asks for a recursive answer
event.summary: www.example.test A leaves the client with RD=1.
event.detail: The application-facing stub resolver asks its configured recursive resolver to finish the job. Recursion Desired is set on this client-to-resolver query.

allFrames.title: Recursive cache misses
allFrames.summary: No usable answer or delegation is cached for this teaching query.
allFrames.detail: Because the recursive resolver cannot answer from cache, it starts iterative resolution. Upstream queries are not asking those servers to recurse on its behalf.

event.title: Recursive cache misses
event.summary: No usable answer or delegation is cached for this teaching query.
event.detail: Because the recursive resolver cannot answer from cache, it starts iterative resolution. Upstream queries are not asking those servers to recurse on its behalf.

allFrames.title: Recursive asks the root
allFrames.summary: Who knows www.example.test?
allFrames.detail: The recursive resolver begins at the root of the namespace. The root need not know the final A record; it only needs to direct the resolver toward the next zone cut.

event.title: Recursive follows the .test delegation

allFrames.title: .test refers to example.test

allFrames.title: Recursive reaches the authoritative zone

allFrames.detail: The delegation chain has reached the authoritative source for the queried name. This server can provide the final A record instead of another referral.

event.title: Recursive reaches the authoritative zone
event.summary: Now the resolver asks the server that owns example.test.
event.detail: The delegation chain has reached the authoritative source for the queried name. This server can provide the final A record instead of another referral.

allFrames.title: Authoritative answer returns
allFrames.summary: www.example.test → 203.0.113.42 · TTL 300s
allFrames.detail: The authoritative response supplies the final address record. The TTL gives downstream caches an upper bound on how long this data may be reused without asking again.

event.title: Authoritative answer returns

allFrames.title: Recursive caches the answer

event.title: Two responses begin concurrently
event.summary: Both lanes serve /hero.jpg and /app.js at the same time.

event.h3Label: H3 request streams 0 + 4 are independent QUIC streams

event.h3Label: QUIC delivers ordered bytes within each stream

allFrames.title: The same logical Stream A data is lost

state.phaseLabel: THE SAME LOGICAL STREAM A DATA IS LOST

event.title: The same logical Stream A data is lost
event.summary: A transport packet carrying /hero.jpg data disappears in each lane.
event.detail: The loss event is synchronized to isolate the transport difference. The comparison is curated; packetization details are chosen to expose head-of-line behavior clearly.
event.h2Label: TCP sequence hole opens in the connection byte stream
event.h3Label: QUIC Stream A offset range is missing

allFrames.title: Later data arrives after the gap

state.phaseLabel: LATER DATA ARRIVES AFTER THE GAP

event.title: Later data arrives after the gap
event.summary: Packets carrying later bytes—including Stream B data—still reach the receiver.
event.detail: The network can deliver packets out of order. What matters is what the transport is allowed to release upward to the HTTP layer.
event.h2Label: Later TCP bytes are buffered behind the missing sequence range
event.h3Label: Stream B bytes can be delivered independently of Stream A ordering

allFrames.title: The lanes visibly diverge
allFrames.summary: HTTP/2 stalls both responses; HTTP/3 keeps /app.js moving.

event.title: The lanes visibly diverge
event.summary: HTTP/2 stalls both responses; HTTP/3 keeps /app.js moving.
event.detail: TCP presents one ordered byte stream, so a sequence gap prevents later connection bytes from reaching HTTP/2. QUIC has no ordering relationship between bytes on different streams, so Stream B can progress while Stream A waits for repair.
event.h2Label: CONNECTION HOL · Stream A + Stream B blocked
event.h3Label: Stream A blocked · Stream B still progressing

allFrames.title: TCP retransmits the missing connection bytes
allFrames.summary: Repairing the TCP sequence hole finally lets HTTP/2 see the buffered later bytes.

state.phaseLabel: TCP RETRANSMITS THE MISSING CONNECTION BYTES

event.title: TCP retransmits the missing connection bytes
event.summary: Repairing the TCP sequence hole finally lets HTTP/2 see the buffered later bytes.
event.detail: Once the missing range arrives, TCP can release the contiguous byte stream. HTTP/2 can then resume parsing frames from both logical streams.
event.h2Label: TCP retransmission repairs the connection byte stream
event.h3Label: Stream B has already moved ahead

allFrames.title: HTTP/2 releases both stalled streams
allFrames.summary: /hero.jpg and /app.js jump forward together after TCP repair.

event.title: HTTP/2 releases both stalled streams
event.summary: /hero.jpg and /app.js jump forward together after TCP repair.
event.detail: This is transport head-of-line blocking beneath HTTP/2 multiplexing: independent HTTP streams were coupled by the ordered TCP substrate.
event.h2Label: Buffered H2 frames become deliverable
event.h3Label: No equivalent cross-stream release event was necessary

allFrames.title: QUIC repairs Stream A
allFrames.summary: /hero.jpg receives the missing stream range while /app.js is already near completion.

event.title: QUIC repairs Stream A
event.summary: /hero.jpg receives the missing stream range while /app.js is already near completion.
event.detail: QUIC retransmits stream data as needed, but the lost Stream A range does not impose ordering on Stream B. STREAM frame boundaries need not be preserved during retransmission.
event.h2Label: Both H2 streams are progressing again
event.h3Label: Only Stream A needed ordering repair

allFrames.title: Both lanes complete
allFrames.summary: The final payload bytes are the same; the delivery coupling under loss was not.

event.title: Both lanes complete
event.summary: The final payload bytes are the same; the delivery coupling under loss was not.
event.detail: This theater isolates transport head-of-line behavior. It does not claim HTTP/3 can never block: flow control, congestion control, or QPACK dependencies can still create delays. This curated trace avoids dynamic QPACK dependencies.
event.h2Label: HTTP/2 complete after connection-level repair
event.h3Label: HTTP/3 complete with independent stream progress
